packageCheck.scope: Packaged runtime and embedded assets only. No window, game code or gameplay validation.

implementation: BuildBreakpoint creates the same original trampoline/unwind image as the relative-jump planner, with a one-byte CC patch and no near-relay requirement.

Router prepares five full-body fingerprints and immutable targets, pins callback modules, registers a resident VEH, then conditionally replaces each first byte with an 8-bit compare-exchange. No remaining instruction bytes change.
The x64 handler only routes owned EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT records with matching exception address and RIP. It changes RIP only and performs no allocation, locking, native original call or memory probe.
Partial publication, cache/protection failures, a debugger or code drift fault confidence. Already published routes continue forwarding; production has no teardown or reset.
Typed STATUS wrappers observe before the native writes, forward once outside the metadata lock, preserve integer arguments/returns and LastError, and drain through finally on native SEH.
Observer bootstrap cannot acquire or compare ownership. Arming requires an external proven barrier and no tracked calls. The barrier itself is not supplied by these components.

tests.scope: Fresh root MSVC runs; private executable memory, real Windows VEH/unwind APIs, synthetic STATUS pools and native test callbacks. No game process or game code executed.

productionCompile: The runner separately compiles the real MEM_IMAGE-only Router without KH2_STATUS_BREAKPOINT_TESTS; compile-only, not executed.
concurrencyProbe: Four native test threads execute original private functions before and during all five entry-byte changes. Every result is the original or wrapped result. Native LOCK INC counters equal total completed calls after join; instruction tails remain exact. A separate four-thread probe starts after publication.
limitations: Resident entry routing does not prove pre-existing native writer calls have drained. No game installer or ownership transaction is connected to TrainerBridge yet.
Tests demonstrate the exercised Windows execution paths, not universal hardware, debugger, exception-handler or arbitrary mod compatibility.
A later handler that consumes owned breakpoints or foreign code executing our original trampolines outside the wrappers is outside the observation contract.
Caller must supply the exact pinned STATUS definitions, fully bound wrappers, RX originals with registered unwind metadata, and process-long object/module lifetimes.
Runtime code drift faults metadata; it cannot make externally corrupted native code safe to execute.
Production has no removal API because a handler or wrapper can already be in flight. Test teardown requires joined callers in its isolated process.
next: Implement and verify the native bootstrap drain, bind the actual five entries/pool/Actor lifetime, then add durable typed field receipts and replace legacy timed scalar cleanup.
